newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: U.S. wheat official sees firm white wheat prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. wheat official sees firm white wheat prices.

text.p: A U.S. wheat official urged Asian buyers on Monday to buy their soft white wheat supplies before prices head up if Pakistan steps into the market.
Tom Mick, the chief executive officer of the Washington Wheat Commission, told a wheat conference in Singapore that soft white wheat prices may rise if Pakistan begins its buying programme.
"The key factor you should be watching now is Pakistan," he said. "Prices should strengthen" if Pakistani buyers came into the market.
Some 90 percent of U.S. white wheat is sold in Asia, Mick added.
Pakistan is the leading buyer of U.S. soft white wheat followed by Japan, the Philippines and South Korea.

Mick said production this year of soft white, planted mainly in Washington, Idaho and parts of Oregon, should reach 7.9 million tonnes in the 1996/97 (June/May) marketing year. Output in 1995/96 reached 8.9 million tonnes.
"We will have, for the seventh year in a row, a fantastic crop," he said. "This is an ideal time to buy your white wheat."
But some dealers expressed doubts whether Pakistan could begin their buying programme immediately.
"In a word, the Pakistanis are a little short on money. They'll have to sort that out first," one dealer said.
